calls.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Predators near the bottom. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Predators’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Predators snap Kochetkov’s ten-game win streak
paras: Nick Perbix struck first for the Predators midway through the first, and Roman Josi pushed the lead to 2-0 early in the second. Jackson Blake got the Hurricanes on the board midway through the period, but that was as close as they got. Adam Edström made it 3-1 for the Predators early in the third, and Ross Colton added an empty-net goal with 41 seconds left to make it 4-1.

The Predators were outshot 30-20, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Juuse Saros made 29 saves for the Preds, and Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 16 of 19 at the other end. It was Kochetkov’s first loss of the season, after ten straight wins to open it. The Predators moved to 6-4-5 and climbed to fifth in the Central, while the Hurricanes dropped to 12-3-2, still first in the NHL in points.
